label: June 2026
subject: Summer '26, AI shopping agents, and the Scripts switch-off
preview: What AI agents need before they recommend you, why answering questions earlier converts, and the June 30 deadline.
intro: June was busy. Shopify's Summer '26 Edition landed on June 17 with a long list of updates, and Shopify Scripts stop running on June 30. If you only read one section this month, read the platform one.

sections.heading: AI agents need facts, not adjectives
sections.short: What AI shopping agents need from you
paragraphs: Summer '26 leaned heavily into what Shopify calls agentic commerce. By default, your products are shared with AI channels through the Shopify Catalog, so assistants can find and compare them without you doing anything.

What they cannot do is guess. An agent comparing three similar products will lean towards the one with clear sizes, materials, delivery times and return terms. 'Premium quality' tells it nothing. '100% linen, ships in 2 days, 30-day returns' tells it plenty.
sections.pullquote: An AI agent can only recommend what it can confirm.

sections.heading: Answer the question before it becomes a doubt
paragraphs: Stores that convert well rarely have more information than everyone else. They put it earlier. Sizing next to the size selector, delivery next to the button, returns in one line rather than a separate page.
Hesitation builds while a buyer goes looking for an answer. The shorter that search, the fewer people give up.

bullets.text: Shopify Scripts stop running on June 30. Anything still built on Scripts, such as tiered discounts or hidden shipping rates, will silently stop working. Check before the end of the month, not after.
bullets.label: Shopify changelog

bullets.text: The Summer '26 Edition (June 17) included more than 150 updates. Coverage highlighted native testing for themes and checkout, more flexible theme blocks in Horizon, and AI channels becoming a standard part of every store.
bullets.label: Shopify Editions

bullets.text: Google's May core update finished in early June. If traffic dipped in late May, compare the full weeks after June 2 before changing anything.
bullets.label: Search Status Dashboard

sections.heading: Make your policy pages pull their weight
paragraphs: Shipping, returns and sizing pages are now read by buyers and by AI systems trying to summarise your store. They are worth an afternoon.
bullets: Put an estimated delivery date next to the buy button.
Summarise your returns policy in one sentence on every product page.
Write sizing as text, not only as an image of a chart.
Confirm nothing in your store still depends on Scripts.

closing: That is June. If the Scripts switch-off broke something on your store, reply and say what. I will share the common fixes next month.
